title: Weather Operations Risk Assessment
description: Free Weather Operations Risk Assessment template for aviation you can edit online and download as PDF. Covers weather operations information, weather hazard risk assessment matrix, weather monitoring and warning systems.

Severe Weather Preparedness Checklist

PRE-SEASON PREPARATION:

☐ Weather procedures reviewed and updated ☐ Staff trained on seasonal hazards

☐ Equipment inspected and serviced ☐ Emergency supplies stocked

☐ Communication systems tested ☐ Coordination with met office established

☐ Contingency plans reviewed ☐ Exercises conducted

THUNDERSTORM/LIGHTNING PROCEDURES:

☐ Monitor weather radar continuously ☐ Activate lightning detection system

☐ Issue warnings to all departments ☐ Suspend outdoor activities when lightning within 5 NM

☐ Secure loose equipment ☐ Move GSE to safe areas

☐ Stop fueling operations ☐ Advise flight crews

☐ Prepare for ramp closures ☐ Resume operations 30 min after last lightning

LOW VISIBILITY PROCEDURES:

☐ Activate low visibility plan ☐ Notify all departments

☐ Implement reduced speed limits (10 km/h) ☐ Consider follow-me vehicles for aircraft

☐ Enhance lighting ☐ Increase spotter presence

☐ Review vehicle routes ☐ Brief all personnel

☐ Consider suspending non-essential ops ☐ Monitor visibility trends

HIGH WIND PROCEDURES:

☐ Monitor wind speeds continuously ☐ Issue wind alerts

☐ Secure all GSE (brakes, chocks) ☐ Tie down light equipment

☐ Remove loose items from ramp ☐ Suspend work at height

☐ Position aircraft into wind if possible ☐ Add extra chocks to aircraft

☐ Suspend cargo loading if winds exceed limits ☐ Brief all personnel

WINTER WEATHER PROCEDURES:

☐ Activate snow and ice plan ☐ Ensure deicing fluids stocked

☐ Pre-treat pavements ☐ Clear snow from critical areas

☐ Monitor pavement temperature ☐ Test friction measurements

☐ Brief deicing crews ☐ Coordinate with ATC on runway conditions

☐ Prepare for aircraft ground deicing ☐ Monitor holdover times

HOT WEATHER PROCEDURES:

☐ Activate heat stress program ☐ Provide additional water stations

☐ Schedule frequent breaks ☐ Monitor personnel for heat stress

☐ Provide cooling areas ☐ Adjust work schedules (early mornings)

☐ Monitor tire pressure ☐ Check aircraft performance calculations

☐ Ensure adequate ventilation ☐ Stock additional water on aircraft

Heat Stress Prevention Program

HEAT STRATEGY:

☐ Acclimatization program for new workers ☐ Work/rest cycles based on temperature

☐ Mandatory hydration (minimum 250ml every 20 min) ☐ Shaded rest areas available

☐ Electrolyte replacement available ☐ Cooling stations with fans/misters

☐ Light-colored, breathable uniforms encouraged ☐ Sunscreen provided

HEAT STRESS SYMPTOMS:

☐ Heat rash ☐ Heat cramps ☐ Heat exhaustion ☐ Heat stroke (medical emergency)

EMERGENCY PROCEDURES FOR HEAT STROKE:

1. Call emergency services immediately

2. Move person to cool area

3. Remove excess clothing

4. Cool with water, ice packs, fans

5. Monitor airway, breathing, circulation
